overview: Worley is a global provider of professional project and asset services (consulting, engineering, procurement and construction management) to the energy, chemicals and resources sectors, operating in more than 40 countries with roughly 40,000 employees. It generates revenue through reimbursable and (to a lesser extent) fixed-price contracts across the full asset lifecycle - from early concept and FEED studies through detailed engineering, procurement, construction management, operations support and decommissioning - and has repositioned itself over the past five years so that around 69% of aggregated revenue is now sustainability-related. The company is headquartered in Australia and listed on the ASX (WOR), having roughly doubled in scale via the 2019 acquisition of Jacobs' Energy, Chemicals and Resources (ECR) division and rebranded from WorleyParsons to Worley.

business_model.summary: Worley earns fees from consulting, engineering, procurement and construction management (EPCM) services, plus license fees, process technology and catalyst sales from its Comprimo and Chemetics technology businesses. The large majority of work (77% of FY2026 revenue) is delivered under reimbursable (cost-plus) contracts that pass through material/subcontractor costs with margin, which structurally limits capital intensity and fixed-price risk; the company explicitly refuses to bid competitive lump-sum turnkey (LSTK) work. Revenue is project- and program-based rather than subscription-recurring, but a large, growing backlog ($13.8bn at FY2026 year-end) and multi-year framework/alliance agreements with major operators provide revenue visibility over 1-3+ year horizons.

revenue_streams.name: Energy (oil, gas, LNG, power, hydrogen, data centers)
Resources (minerals, metals, fertilizers, energy transition materials, water, complex critical infrastructure)
Chemicals (refining, petrochemicals, specialty chemicals, direct air capture)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - large multinational and national energy, chemicals, resources and infrastructure operators (e.g., bp, APA Group, BHP, Venture Global, Oxy/1PointFive, INPEX, CNOOC); highly diversified customer base with no single customer representing a significant share of revenue or profit
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~52% of regional aggregated revenue, Europe/Middle East/Africa (EMEA) ~37%, Asia-Pacific (APAC) ~11%; reports financials in Australian dollars (functional/presentation currency) while a majority of revenue and costs are earned in USD and other currencies, creating FX translation effects on reported results

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global engineering/EPCM firms serving energy, chemicals and resources, with leading positions in several core markets (LNG/integrated gas, sulphur recovery and sulphuric acid process technology via Comprimo and Chemetics, and a long track record in major resources and petrochemical projects); scale roughly doubled by the 2019 Jacobs ECR acquisition, giving it a top-tier position alongside Fluor, KBR and Jacobs in global EPCM

moat_factors.factor: Deep, long-standing customer relationships and framework/alliance agreements
moat_factors.description: Multi-year global strategic alliances (e.g., with bp) and repeat work with major operators (APA, BHP, Oxy) create switching costs and repeat-business visibility, reflected in a growing backlog

Worley Comprimo (sulphur recovery/gas treating, 1,200+ licensed units) and Worley Chemetics (sulphuric acid, 310+ plants) hold 100+ active patents, providing licensing revenue and a technical differentiator that is hard to replicate

moat_factors.factor: Global scale and integrated delivery network
moat_factors.description: 40+ country footprint and Global Integrated Delivery (GID) centers in India and Colombia (5,089 people, 14.5% of project hours) give cost-competitive, scalable engineering capacity for large, complex, multi-region programs

Deliberate avoidance of competitively bid lump-sum turnkey (LSTK) work, with 77% of revenue on reimbursable contracts, reduces downside execution risk relative to some EPC-heavy peers, though it also caps upside margin capture

Long operating history (formerly WorleyParsons) and recognized sustainability leadership support pre-qualification on large capital programs, though the industry has relatively low switching costs on any single project

weaknesses: No hard network effects or strong pricing power - engineering/EPCM services face competitive tendering and margin pressure from multiple credible global peers

Margins are thin and sensitive to project mix (construction/fabrication/procurement work dilutes margin versus higher-value consulting/FEED work), as evidenced by the FY2026 EBITA margin decline to 6.1% from 6.8%
Geopolitical and single-region concentration risk - the Middle East conflict alone cut FY2026 underlying EBITA by roughly $58 million
Labor-intensive, people-driven business exposed to talent attraction/retention costs and wage inflation across 40+ countries
AUD reporting currency creates translation volatility on USD/other-currency-denominated earnings, obscuring underlying operating performance

growth_drivers: Energy transition and decarbonization work - sustainability-related revenue rose from ~30% to ~69% of aggregated revenue over five years, with an original aspiration of 75%

Priority growth markets: integrated gas/LNG, energy transition materials (copper, lithium, nickel, rare earths, battery materials), and complex critical infrastructure (data centers, power, nuclear, industrial water, ports/terminals)
Scaling 'full project delivery' (moving further into EPC/EPCM execution, not just FEED/consulting) to capture more value across the asset lifecycle on larger, more complex programs
Digital and AI-enabled delivery - $70 million planned investment over two years to embed AI/digital tools, targeting productivity, margin durability and competitive differentiation

Growing backlog - $13.8 billion at FY2026 year-end, up from $12.7 billion in FY2025 (18% growth on a constant-currency basis), including progress on major projects such as Venture Global's CP2 LNG (Final Investment Decision reached on both phases)
Management's medium-term ambition (set at the May 2026 Investor Day) targets double-digit underlying EBITA growth through FY2030 and an underlying EBITA margin (excluding procurement) of 9.0-9.5%
Cost-out program exceeded its original $100 million target, delivering $132 million in savings to offset inflation and fund reinvestment
Ongoing capital return program (buybacks and dividends) signaling management confidence in cash generation

business.description: Ongoing regional conflict has caused supply chain disruption, delayed customer investment decisions, and cut FY2026 underlying EBITA by roughly $58 million; management flags continued uncertainty and second-order supply chain effects (e.g., sulphur supply for North African fertilizer projects) persisting into FY2027
Failure to execute large, complex projects on time/budget could trigger contract disputes, financial loss and reputational damage, curtailing future project awards
New entrants, alternative capital/delivery models and maturing competition (including emerging full-service providers) could compress margins, erode market share or lead to unfavorable contract terms
A people-intensive business model in a competitive global labor market for engineering talent; failure to attract/retain skilled staff could constrain growth and delivery capability

financial.description: Gearing (net debt/(net debt+equity)) rose to 26.4% at FY2026 year-end from 20.9% in FY2025, alongside declining operating cash flow ($401m vs $741m in FY2025) and continued share buybacks, warranting monitoring of balance sheet flexibility

Reports in AUD while earning a majority of revenue in USD and other currencies; a strengthening Australian dollar was cited as a direct headwind to FY2026 reported results and remains a translation risk into FY2027

Project-based working capital (receivables, unbilled revenue, provisions) can create cash flow timing volatility; normalized cash conversion was within the 85-95% target range in FY2026 but operating cash flow nearly halved year-on-year

regulatory.description: Mandatory climate-related disclosures under AASB S2 and evolving global ESG reporting standards (ESRS double materiality assessment adopted FY2026) add compliance cost and disclosure risk

regulatory.risk: Data privacy, AI governance and cybersecurity regulation
regulatory.description: Increasing regulatory complexity around data protection, cross-border data flows and responsible AI use as the company scales AI-enabled service delivery

regulatory.risk: Sanctions, trade restrictions and modern slavery/human rights compliance
regulatory.description: Operations in 40+ countries, including higher-risk geographies, expose the company to sanctions regimes, export controls and supply-chain labor practice risk

macro.description: Revenue is ultimately driven by customers' capital expenditure decisions in energy, chemicals and resources, which are cyclical and sensitive to commodity prices, interest rates and geopolitical risk appetite

Trade restrictions, sanctions, political instability and regional conflicts (Middle East being the current acute example) can delay or cancel projects and disrupt supply chains and commodity/FX markets

Higher-for-longer interest rates can raise customers' cost of capital and delay final investment decisions on large, long-duration capital projects, indirectly slowing Worley's project pipeline conversion

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global engineering/EPCM demand is underpinned by structural themes: energy security and affordability, critical minerals and resource security, decarbonization/energy transition investment, and a fast-growing complex critical infrastructure sub-sector (data centers, power, nuclear). Management characterizes underlying medium- and long-term demand fundamentals as favorable despite near-term Middle East-related disruption.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - tied to the capital investment cycles of energy, chemicals and resources customers, which move with commodity prices, global growth and geopolitical risk appetite; reimbursable contract structure (77% of revenue) partially smooths volatility relative to fixed-price EPC-heavy peers
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate and indirect - higher rates raise customers' cost of capital, potentially slowing final investment decisions on large projects, rather than directly affecting Worley's own funding costs (which are more modest given a non-capital-intensive service model)
key_input_costs: Skilled engineering labor (wages/salaries are the largest cost line)
Reimbursable project materials and subcontractor costs (largely passed through to customers with minimal margin risk)

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: aggregated revenue $12,023m (down 0.2%), underlying EBITA $734m (down 11% YoY, down 6.1% ex-FX), underlying EBITA margin fell to 6.1% from 6.8%; NPATA $306m (down 36%); operating cash flow $401m (down from $741m); backlog grew to $13.8bn (from $12.7bn, +18% constant currency); shares fell over 11% on the day amid the earnings miss
Worley increased its expected FY2026 Middle East conflict EBITA impact to up to $60 million, up from an earlier $30-40 million estimate flagged in April 2026, triggering a further share price decline

Investor Day: management set a medium-term ambition for double-digit underlying EBITA growth through FY2030 and an FY2026 underlying EBITA margin (ex-procurement) target of 9.0-9.5%; announced a new $300 million on-market share buyback and $70 million AI/digital investment plan over two years
Completed the $500 million on-market share buyback first announced in February 2025

Restructured Western Europe operations in response to softer market conditions, part of broader repositioning of resources toward higher-demand markets; cost-out program delivered $132 million in savings, exceeding the original $100 million target

New contract wins/extensions including a five-year EPC renewal with CNOOC (UK North Sea), support for INPEX's Abadi LNG Project in Indonesia, an ARENA renewable hydrogen advisory study, and an engineering services award from D-CRBN for a renewable syngas plant in Belgium
Board appointment - Jeanne Johns joined the Board effective 1 September 2025 (Audit and Risk Committee, Nominations Committee)

Group Executive changes: Kirsten Bruner appointed Chief People Officer (April 2026); Adrian Smith, Karen Furlani and Sue Brown departed the Group Executive; Andy Hemingway and Mark Trueman took on expanded leadership roles effective 1 July 2026

Revenue phasing expected to be broadly even across the two half-year periods

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Chris Ashton acknowledged FY2026 underlying EBITA declined due to softer market conditions, Middle East conflict-related disruption and delayed customer investment, and AUD strengthening. Management expects Middle East work volumes to lift through FY2027 as the year progresses, though timing/scale of the recovery remains difficult to predict. Confidence in the FY2027 outlook is underpinned by strengthening activity in North America (the largest market), a growing major-projects pipeline, and continued progress on the FY2030 double-digit EBITA growth ambition. Chair John Grill emphasized disciplined capital management, governance and risk management frameworks evolving alongside growth into larger, more complex projects.

bull_case: Large, growing backlog ($13.8bn, +18% constant currency) provides multi-year revenue visibility and supports management's FY2027 mid-to-high single-digit growth guidance

Structural, multi-decade demand tailwinds across energy security, critical minerals/resources, and decarbonization/energy transition investment, further diversified into fast-growing complex critical infrastructure (data centers, power, nuclear)
Disciplined reimbursable-contract model (77% of revenue) and explicit avoidance of lump-sum turnkey risk reduces the probability of large project losses relative to some EPC-heavy peers

Management has articulated a credible medium-term ambition (double-digit underlying EBITA growth to FY2030) backed by a cost-out program that has already exceeded its target, plus continued capital returns (buybacks, stable dividend) signaling confidence in cash generation

Current valuation reflects a depressed FY2026 earnings base (Middle East disruption, FX headwind, one-off restructuring) that could normalize as the conflict resolves and North American activity strengthens, offering potential earnings recovery upside
bear_case: FY2026 results show clear margin erosion (underlying EBITA margin down to 6.1% from 6.8%) and a sharp operating cash flow decline (down ~46% to $401m), raising questions about near-term earnings quality and cash conversion durability

Middle East conflict impact was repeatedly underestimated and upgraded through FY2026 (from $30-40m to $60m), highlighting execution/guidance credibility risk and the company's exposure to unpredictable geopolitical shocks

Rising leverage (gearing up to 26.4% from 20.9%) combined with continued share buybacks during a period of declining operating cash flow could pressure balance sheet flexibility if market conditions do not improve as management expects

Intensely competitive global EPCM industry (Jacobs, Fluor, KBR, Bechtel, Wood Group, and emerging full-service entrants) limits structural pricing power and could compress margins further, especially as the company leans into lower-margin construction/fabrication/procurement-heavy project delivery

AUD reporting currency creates persistent translation volatility on predominantly USD-denominated earnings, and a further strengthening Australian dollar remains a stated headwind into FY2027 independent of underlying operational performance
